Here is a concise overview of how the **Vercel** Cursor plugin fits together and how you use it.

## What it is

The plugin bundles **guidance** (skills), **automation** (commands), **optional delegation** (subagents), **lifecycle hooks**, and a **Vercel MCP server** so Cursor can both *advise* on Vercel/Next.js topics and *act* on your linked project when authenticated.

## How the pieces work

| Piece | How it works |
|--------|----------------|
| **Skills** | Topic experts (AI SDK, deployments, env vars, Next.js, Turbopack, etc.). The agent can load them when your task matches; you can also invoke them with `/` if your setup exposes skill commands. |
| **Subagents** | Specialized agents (e.g. deployment, performance, AI architecture) for heavier or scoped work; same idea—automatic or `/` where supported. |
| **Commands** | Slash commands such as `/deploy`, `/env`, `/status`, `/bootstrap`, `/marketplace`, `/conventions`. They run scripted flows (deploy, sync env, check project status, etc.). |
| **Hooks** | `SessionStart` / `SessionEnd` run automatically around sessions—no action needed unless you customize them. |
| **Rules** | Project/workspace rules that apply automatically when configured. |
| **MCP server (`vercel`)** | Exposes tools the assistant can call (listings, deployments, env, etc.). This is what turns “talk about Vercel” into “query or change things on the platform” **after** you authenticate. |

## Typical flow for you

1. **Ask in chat** — e.g. “why did production fail?” or “pull prod env locally.” The agent uses skills + MCP tools when relevant.
2. **Use `/` commands** — e.g. `/status` or `/deploy prod` for the bundled workflows.
3. **Authenticate MCP once** — so tool calls to Vercel succeed.

## Authentication (required for MCP)

Per `STATUS.md` in the Vercel MCP server folder, the **plugin-vercel-vercel** MCP server **needs authentication**. In Cursor, that is done by invoking the **`mcp_auth`** tool for server **`plugin-vercel-vercel`** with an empty object `{}` so you can complete the login/consent flow in the UI.

Until you do that, overview and skills still help; **platform actions** (deployments, env sync via MCP, etc.) may be limited.

---

**Summary:** Skills and rules guide behavior; slash commands run packaged workflows; hooks run in the background; the **Vercel MCP server** extends the agent with real Vercel operations after **`mcp_auth`** for `plugin-vercel-vercel`.
